title: Spanish café A1
targetPerformance: Complete a six-turn café exchange in Spanish: greet, introduce yourself, order a drink politely, ask its price, understand a price from 1 to 100, and thank the server; satisfy at least 5 of 6 checks in two roleplays.
whyItMatters: Use a small set of reusable phrases in a real café interaction.

subskills.title: Greet and introduce yourself
subskills.why: Open a short exchange with familiar words.
subskills.selfCorrection: Check the time-of-day greeting and say the name aloud once.

subskills.title: Order café basics
subskills.why: Ask for a drink and food with useful sentence frames.
subskills.selfCorrection: Check the drink noun, article, and a polite ending.

subskills.title: Read numbers and prices
subskills.why: Recognize quantities and ask what something costs.
subskills.selfCorrection: Read the amount back and distinguish euros from céntimos.
drills: Say a price with euros or dollars.

subskills.title: Choose ser or estar
subskills.why: Use identity and temporary location/state forms.
subskills.selfCorrection: Ask whether the sentence gives identity, a location, or a current state.
drills: Contrast es with está in café sentences.

subskills.title: Make polite requests
subskills.why: Ask a server for an item using a complete question.
subskills.selfCorrection: Check who is addressed: puede for usted, das for tú.

subskills.title: Complete a café visit
subskills.why: Connect the phrases into a short practical exchange.
subskills.selfCorrection: Check all six target actions, then retry one missed turn.
drills: Change one menu item and price.

resources.title: WordReference Spanish-English
resources.why: Look up café vocabulary and examples.

barriers.fix: Say each short phrase quietly once, then try the exchange; retries count.

barriers.barrier: Too many new words at once
barriers.fix: Start with café, té, agua, pan, and the same two request frames.
Practice accented spelling, but accept listed unaccented variants during fast rounds.
